quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: When should you reduce your speed?

options.text: When the road is icy.
When there is dense fog.
When it is raining.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Only drive at the maximum speed limit in ideal conditions. You must slow down when weather is bad, such as snow, ice, rain, or fog.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn.
Turn right at the intersection.
Parking area ahead.
A crossroad is ahead. Watch for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: A crossroad is ahead. Watch for traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is coming.

questions.question: You should not cross railroad tracks if there is not room for your entire vehicle on the other side.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Never cross railroad tracks unless your entire vehicle will fit on the other side. Never stop on the tracks. Wait until there is enough space for your whole vehicle to clear the tracks.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a crash?

options.text: Wear your seat belt.
Only drive on weekdays.
Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.
Only drive between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear your seat belt.
questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the single best thing you can do to protect yourself from injury or death in a crash.

questions.question: Which substances can impair your driving and result in a DUII arrest?

options.text: Beer, wine, and liquor
Controlled substances, such as illegal drugs or prescription medicines
Inhalants, such as glue or paint
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Many substances can impair your driving. These include alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and some prescription and over-the-counter medicines.

questions.question: What should you do if an aggressive driver cuts you off?

options.text: Call the police right away.
Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.
Flash your lights to show the driver they are wrong.
Drive aggressively back to get even.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and get out of the aggressive driver's way. Trying to get revenge makes the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: What documents must you show when stopped by police?

options.text: Proof of insurance.
Your driver's license.
Proof of registration.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must have your driver's license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance in your vehicle at all times. You must show all three when stopped by police.

questions.question: If you are angry after an argument, what should you do before driving?

options.text: Play loud music so you don't think about it.
Take a few minutes to calm down.
Drive on the interstate to let off steam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down.
questions.explanation: Your emotions affect your ability to drive safely. If you are angry, excited, afraid, or upset, calm down before driving. You need to focus on the road.

questions.question: If a green traffic light is on but a police officer signals you to stop, what should you do?

options.text: Obey the officer.
Obey the traffic signal.
Do what the car in front of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey the officer.
questions.explanation: Always obey a police officer's directions, even if they conflict with traffic signals or signs.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: You should use cruise control near railroad crossings to keep a steady speed.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to stop.
You have the right-of-way at railroad crossings and do not need to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to stop.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal. Always be careful near railroad tracks.

questions.question: How should a seat belt be adjusted?

options.text: Loose.
Snug across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Hidden beneath the seat.
To stop the seat belt alarm from working.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snug across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should be comfortable so you can fit your fist between it and your chest.

questions.question: Why is using a cell phone while driving a distraction?

options.text: It makes drivers worry about call costs.
It takes your hands, eyes, and attention away from driving.
It distracts other drivers on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes your hands, eyes, and attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Cell phone use while driving is dangerous because it takes your eyes, hands, and focus away from the road. Even experienced drivers increase their crash risk when using a phone while driving.

questions.question: If traffic is blocking an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Drive close behind the car in front in case the light turns red.
Honk to make traffic move.
Wait until you can cross the entire intersection before entering it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can cross the entire intersection before entering it.
questions.explanation: Never enter an intersection unless you can drive all the way through it. In heavy traffic, wait for vehicles ahead to clear the intersection so you do not block cross traffic when the light changes.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving in bad weather?

options.text: A sudden weather change requires a change in your driving.
Slow down when driving in rain and fog.
Watch closely for vehicles coming up behind you in bad weather.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When weather changes suddenly, adjust your driving. Always slow down in rain and fog. Watch for vehicles behind you that may be driving too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a stopped school bus with its stop arm out?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk and pass on the left side.
Continue driving when you think children are done exiting.
Pass before the bus door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when a school bus shows its stop signal. Do not move until the stop arm is pulled in.

questions.question: What should you do before starting the car?

options.text: Fasten your safety belt.
Make sure all passengers have fastened their safety belts.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive without a safety belt. Always fasten your belt and make sure all passengers do the same before driving. Safety belts greatly reduce your risk of injury or death in a crash.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a detour ahead.
You must stop for flaggers.
The road is closed.
Construction or road work is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Construction or road work is ahead.
questions.explanation: Construction signs are orange with black text. They warn drivers of unusual or dangerous conditions ahead. Slow down and drive carefully in work zones.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Crossroad ahead.
Flagger ahead.
Lane ends.
Turn right or go straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossroad ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to hazards ahead. This sign warns you of an upcoming intersection.

questions.question: What do "No passing zone" signs tell drivers?

options.text: Speed up slightly.
It is not safe to pass.
Keep a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is not safe to pass.
questions.explanation: You cannot pass in a "No passing zone." These areas have poor visibility or other conditions that make passing unsafe.

questions.question: If pedestrians cross in the middle of the street instead of in a crosswalk, must you stop?

options.text: Yes, you must stop.
No, you do not have to stop.
Honk your horn at them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, you must stop.
questions.explanation: You must always stop for pedestrians, even if they are crossing illegally. Pedestrian safety comes first.

questions.question: You want to turn right at a corner. A pedestrian with a guide dog is about to cross in front of you. What should you do?

options.text: Turn off your engine while the person crosses.
Tell the pedestrian when to cross.
Wait for the person to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the person to cross.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians with guide dogs or white canes always have the right-of-way. You must let them cross before you proceed.

questions.question: A school bus ahead on your side of the road has its red lights flashing. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down to no more than 10 mph.
Stop and wait until the lights stop flashing.
Change lanes and pass carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has red lights flashing and a stop arm out, you must stop completely. Do not move until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is put away. Never pass a school bus that is loading or unloading students.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Traffic from the right will be merging into your lane.
Always stop.
A divided highway is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic from the right will be merging into your lane.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you that traffic will merge into your lane from the right. Be ready to make room for these vehicles to merge safely.

questions.question: When driving on major highways, what should you do?

options.text: Stay alert.
Keep your eyes moving.
Be ready to react to hazards.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: On highways, stay alert and keep your eyes moving. Do not stare at one spot for more than a few seconds. Be ready to react quickly to any hazards.

questions.question: If a vehicle has airbags, should you wear a seat belt?

options.text: Yes, seat belts should still be worn.
No, seat belts are not needed.
Seat belts should be worn behind your back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, seat belts should still be worn.
questions.explanation: Airbags are an important safety feature. For the best protection, always wear both lap and shoulder belts together with airbags.
